title: Standard ETAS aftershock tails overpredicted Oklahoma M3+ earthquakes in 2019-2026 by about 4 times; an Omori law with a 1.4-2.2 year exponential taper contained the observed counts
abstract: Question: is the 2021-2026 residual earthquake rate in Oklahoma an aftershock tail of the 2010-2020 earthquakes, or an independent rate that injection still drives, and which model forecasts it? Approach: we fit a space-time ETAS model with a quarterly, spatially varying background to the Oklahoma Geological Survey catalog, 2010-2026 (3,045 events of M 3.0 or more; 10,855 of M 2.5 or more), with EM estimation. We made forecasts from 2019-07 and 2021-01 with fits to earlier data only, and we checked the method on synthetic catalogs. Results: the standard ETAS model (Omori exponent p near 1) fit to 2010-2020 forecast 391 (95% range 273-521) M3+ events in 2021-2026 from earlier events alone; 102 occurred. From 2019-07 it forecast 704 (536-926); 179 occurred. Even fit to all data, it expected 104 direct aftershocks of pre-2021 events in 2021-2026, but assigned only 35. An exponential taper on the Omori law increased the log-likelihood by 103 (M3+) and 421 (M2.5+) for one parameter, with a taper time of 515-794 days. With a decaying background, the tapered model forecast 59 (22-137) and 157 (85-257) events, and it had the best cell log-likelihood of all tested models, also better than exponential decay of the recent rate. In 2021-2026, about half of the events descend from earlier earthquakes, and the independent rate (4.2 per year) is about 1.4-2.8 times the 1980-2008 rate after correction for a bias found in the synthetic test. Limitations: the taper was added after the standard forecasts failed; only two overlapping forecast starts; mixed OGS magnitudes; no triggering across the box edges.

display.caption: Out-of-sample annual forecasts of M3+ earthquakes in the Oklahoma box from 2019-07 (left) and 2021-01 (right), each fit only to earlier data. The standard ETAS model (blue) and the epoch-productivity model (pink) forecast too many events. The tapered ETAS model with a decaying background (green; shading: 95% simulation range) contains the observed counts (black). Orange: exponential decay of the recent rate. Yellow: tapered cascade of pre-start events only.

Annual M3+ counts (black dots) separated into independent events (blue) and triggered events by the period of their root ancestor, for the tapered (left) and standard (right) ETAS fits to 2010-2026. Dashed line: 1980-2008 rate of all M3+ events in the box (1.52 per year).

Log-likelihood of ETAS variants relative to the standard model (M3+, 2010-2026). The taper of the Omori law gives +103 for one parameter; productivity by epoch gives +18 for four parameters; fixed p values are worse.

We use its ComCat download and parsed OCC disposal tables. Our ETAS background follows disposal with a short memory, which agrees with its finding that pressure loss in 1-4 years was necessary.
